2. Data Ingestion

From Kafka events to Delta Lake — the full ingestion pipeline

  • Kafka5Kafka architecture: partitions, consumer groups, transactions, KRaft. 7T msgs/day at LinkedIn. Scientific examples: genomics event streams, LHC DAQ, environmental sensor feeds.
  • Schema Registry5Confluent Schema Registry + Glue Schema Registry + Iceberg schema evolution. Backward/forward/full compatibility. The type system for the data pipeline.
  • Kafka Connect5Standard pipeline for operational data → lakehouse. Kafka Connect framework + Debezium log-based CDC. 200+ connectors, exactly-once via Kafka transactions.
  • Spark Streaming5Spark Structured Streaming: micro-batch vs continuous, watermarks, stateful ops. Scientific examples: batch+streaming genomics, IoT sensor windows, LHC online monitoring.
  • Big Data IngestCore Big Data & Platform Infrastructure: ingestion at exabyte scale. Mathematical foundations of probabilistic cardinality estimation (HyperLogLog), Delta Lake Z-Ordering for column pruning, and the small-file problem with Auto Compaction + Liquid Clustering. PySpark code templates run real workloads on Delta + S3 + cloudFiles streaming.
  • Ingestion MapCross-page ingestion concept map. Interactive D3 force-directed graph showing the data flow from Kafka through Schema Registry, Spark Streaming, Delta Lake, Auto Compaction, to the HLL materialised view. Each node links to its host page. Hover for flow details, click to navigate.
  • ELT + rETL5Managed ELT ingestion from 14 source systems and reverse-ETL activation back into business tools.
  • HPC + MLQ4 2026 roadmap. Shows how the HPC ingestion pipeline feeds ML feature stores and model training. The full loop: Kafka events → Delta Lake Silver → feature engineering → Feast feature store → distributed training (Ray/Horovod) → MLflow tracking → model registry → serving. Interactive demos via Pyodide.
  • Streaming5Kafka, Pulsar, Flink, Spark Streaming — the Lambda→Kappa evolution from dual-pipeline to unified streaming.
  • Streaming SQL5Streaming SQL: Flink SQL (stream-table duality, temporal joins, windowing), Spark Structured Streaming, Materialize (differential dataflow), RisingWave. Math: watermark, event-time.
  • Flink5Flink deep dive: watermark, state backends, exactly-once, CEP, CDC ingestion. The streaming engine for Iceberg/Delta/Hudi writes. Scientific examples: real-time genomics, LHC trigger, sensor monitoring.
  • Pulsar5Pulsar: segmented storage, geo-replication, functions. Yahoo-origin alternative to Kafka. Scientific examples: multi-region sensor networks, distributed genomics.

3. Storage & Compute

Lakehouses, warehouses, table formats, and query engines

  • Delta5Most widely-deployed open table format. ACID transactions, time travel, Change Data Feed, Z-Order, Liquid Clustering. Production on every Databricks deployment. Transaction-log replay Pyodide demo.
  • Databricks5Spark, PySpark, Delta Lake and the Bronze-Silver-Gold medallion architecture powering analytics at scale.
  • Snowflake5Snowflake serving layer with multi-cluster compute, RBAC and governed SQL for analytics & BI.
  • Iceberg5Netflix-origin open table format with manifest trees, hidden partitioning, time travel, schema evolution. Production at Netflix, Apple, Stripe. SQL+PyIceberg+Trino code, manifest tree diagram, NYC Taxi on Iceberg Pyodide demo.
  • Hudi5Uber-origin open table format for incremental/UPSERT workloads. COW vs MOR table types, CDC ingestion, change-logs. Production at Uber, Walmart, ByteDance. Distinct from Iceberg/Delta because of upsert-first design.
  • Paimon5Flink-first streaming-native table format (2023) with changelog mode + partial-update merge. Treats tables as streams.
  • Glue5Serverless Spark ETL, Data Catalog, Crawlers, Glue Studio, Schema Registry. The most-used data-lake catalog on AWS. Code: Glue PySpark jobs, crawler configs, cross-account catalog access.
  • Databricks LH5Delta + Unity + MLflow + Databricks SQL + Photon end-to-end. Uber, Airbnb, JPMorgan production stack. The most deployed lakehouse platform.
  • Snowflake Polaris5Snowflake's Apache-licensed REST catalog (2024) + Iceberg open lakehouse. Strategic counter-bet to Databricks Unity. Tabular team now at Snowflake.
  • Lakehouse5The lake→lakehouse evolution: Hadoop → S3+Hive → Iceberg/Delta/Hudi. Vendor-neutral open table formats giving ACID + SQL to cheap object storage. Anchor page for the Data Lakehouse group.
  • Lake Formation5Cell-level RLS, LF-tags governance, cross-account data sharing. The most production-deployed lakehouse governance on AWS. IAM for data.
  • Catalogs5Comparison of metadata/catalog systems: AWS Glue Data Catalog, Hive Metastore, Nessie (Git-for-data), Databricks Unity Catalog, Snowflake Polaris, Iceberg REST Catalog. The metadata-layer battle.
  • Tabular5First SaaS Iceberg platform, founded by Iceberg spec authors (Ryan Blue, Daniel Weeks). Acquired by Snowflake 2024. Multi-cloud managed Iceberg.
  • BigQuery5BigQuery deep dive: columnar storage, BI Engine, partitioning, clustering, Materialized Views, BigLake (Iceberg on GCS). Scientific examples: genomics on BigQuery, climate data, NASA datasets.
  • Redshift5Redshift deep dive: columnar, sort keys, distribution styles, Spectrum, Serverless, RA3. Scientific examples: genomics on Redshift, NASA MODIS, climate analytics.
  • ClickHouse5ClickHouse: MergeTree engine, materialised views, real-time ingestion, vectorised execution. Yandex origin. Scientific examples: genomics variant queries, IoT telemetry, time-series analytics.
  • Druid5Sub-second queries on event/time-series data at scale. Netflix, Airbnb, Alibaba use Druid for real-time analytics.
  • Impala5Cloudera-origin MPP SQL engine (2012) for HDFS + Kudu. LLVM JIT codegen. Still relevant for on-prem Hadoop stacks.
  • StarRocks5MySQL-compatible lakehouse query engine (2021 fork of Doris). Vectorised SIMD execution, reads Iceberg/Delta/Hive directly. Fastest Trino alternative for BI.
  • Pinot5LinkedIn-origin real-time OLAP engine with star-tree index for sub-second analytics on billions of rows. 50B events/day at LinkedIn.
  • DuckDB5In-process OLAP that runs anywhere — just open a Parquet file. Arrow-native, OSS, 10× faster than Postgres on a single node.
  • Big Data5BigQuery, DuckDB, Spark Streaming, Flink, Kafka, Pulsar, Iceberg — the modern open + serverless stack with code + free tiers.
  • Arrow5The zero-copy columnar format that makes DuckDB, Polars, Pandas, Spark, Flink interchangeable. Arrow Flight for transfer, C Data Interface for UDFs.
  • Polars vs DuckDB5Three DataFrame libraries benchmarked in your browser. Arrow-native, lazy evaluation, 10-30× speed differences — with Pyodide timing demos.

8. Cross-Domain Math & Living Equations

Elegant Code (the collision) → Living Equations (interactive demos)

  • Elegant Code5 cross-disciplinary scenarios showing how ONE math equation bridges 3+ sciences. SVD (genomics↔audio↔finance), Attention (folding↔NLP), Poisson (sequencing↔networks↔decay), FFT (mass spec↔audio↔cryo-EM), Verlet (MD↔games↔orbits). Code in Scala/Rust/Go/Elixir/Zig. 'X IS Y' insights = the unexpected connections no single PhD sees.
  • Living SVD5Live SVD demo: drag k (number of principal components) and watch Out-of-Africa migration pattern emerge from the 1000-Genomes chr-22 allele-frequency matrix. Pyodide runs the SVD in-browser; recharts visualises the top-k PC scatter. Production bridge: np.linalg.svd.
  • Living Attention5Live Attention demo: drag d_k (head dimension) and watch the attention matrix sharpen from a smear to a contact-map pattern on a UniRef50 multiple sequence alignment. Pyodide computes softmax(QK^T/√d_k)×V in-browser. Production bridge: torch.nn.MultiheadAttention.
  • Living FFT5Live FFT demo: drag N (window size) and watch the 3 notes of a C-major chord (C4, E4, G4) resolve from a smear to 3 sharp spikes. Pyodide computes X[k] = Σx[n]·e^(-2πikn/N) in-browser. Production bridge: np.fft.fft / scipy.fft.
  • Living Poisson5Live Poisson demo: drag λ (mean coverage) and watch P(≥10×) cross 0.95 at λ=14. The Poisson distribution is overlaid on a 1000-Genomes chr-22 read-depth histogram (synthetic). Pyodide computes the PMF and CDF in-browser. Production bridge: scipy.stats.poisson.
  • Living Entropy5Live Entropy demo: drag n (number of bins) and watch H converge to its asymptote as the discrete distribution approaches the underlying continuous density. Computed on gnomAD BRCA1 allele-frequency data (synthetic). Pyodide computes H = -Σp·log(p) in-browser. Production bridge: scipy.stats.entropy.
  • Living Black-Scholes5Live Black-Scholes demo: drag σ (volatility) and watch the SPX 30-day call option price curve steepen from $0 to $50+. Pyodide computes C = S·N(d1) − K·e^(−rT)·N(d2) across strikes. Production bridge: QuantLib.
  • Living Haversine5Live Haversine demo: pick source and destination from 10 major ports and watch the great-circle distance update. Pyodide computes d = 2R·arcsin(√(sin²(Δφ/2) + cos(φ1)·cos(φ2)·sin²(Δλ/2))). Production bridge: geopy / PostGIS.
  • Living Kalman5Live Kalman demo: drag R (measurement noise variance) and watch the filter's tracking smoothness trade off against responsiveness. Pyodide computes x̂(t+1) = x̂(t) + K·(z − H·x̂(t)) on synthetic AIS positions. Production bridge: filterpy / OpenCV KalmanFilter.
  • Living Monte Carlo5Live Monte Carlo demo: drag N (number of GBM paths) and watch the option-price MC estimate converge to the closed-form Black-Scholes value. Pyodide simulates N GBM paths and averages payoffs. Production bridge: QuantLib MC engine.
  • Living GBM5Live GBM demo: drag σ (volatility) and watch 50 simulated SPX 1-year paths fan out wider (high σ) or narrower (low σ). Pyodide integrates dS = μS·dt + σS·dW via Euler discretization. Production bridge: scipy.stats.lognorm / QuantLib GBM.

9. Computational Science

The collision: physics, chemistry, biology, climate, fintech, and more

  • Quantum5AI illustrations + circuit short, qubit superposition + Hadamard/CNOT/Pauli gates + Bell states + VQE variational principle + Grover O(√N) + QFT, low-level PyTorch QuantumGate+QuantumCircuit+VQE+GroverCircuit.

  • ClimateFrom CMIP6 global circulation models to regional downscaling, from 100-year flood VaR to drought probability. The natural home for the VaR and Bayes cards when they're applied to climate scenarios. Covers reanalysis (ERA5), emissions scenarios (SSP/RCP), and the generalized extreme value (GEV) distribution.
  • ML PlaygroundInteractive ML model training in-browser via Pyodide + scikit-learn. Adjust hyperparameters (tree depth, number of trees, learning rate, feature selection) via sliders, click Train, and watch the ROC curve, loss curve, feature importance, and confusion matrix update in real-time. Three datasets: LHC jet tagging, genomics variant calling, finance fraud detection.

Referenced obliquely in multiple DeeperThoughts — this page gives it a host. Critical for 'did the treatment cause the outcome' questions across A/B tests, policy evaluation, and ML fairness.

The maritime host for cross-disciplinary elegant-code cards.

Covers all 7 analysis types: preprocessing, EDA, feature engineering, machine learning (BDT/CNN/GNN), statistical inference, Monte Carlo simulation, and real-time trigger analysis. Each card: math equation + runnable Python (Pyodide) + Recharts visualization. Trend detection angle: Mann-Kendall, Sen's slope, changepoint detection, GEV, attribution analysis. Uses CMIP6 scenarios, NOAA GHCN, ERA5 (Copernicus CDS).
  • Space Data AnalysisA comprehensive, multi-layered data science analysis of astronomical datasets. Covers all 5 levels of granularity — from raw JWST/TESS/Gaia photon counts through calibrated spectra, light curves, aggregated catalogs, ML classification (star/galaxy/quasar, exoplanet detection), to interactive visualizations. Each card: math equation + runnable Python (Pyodide) + Recharts visualization. Classification angle: SVM, Random Forest, BDT, CNN on images, GNN on celestial catalogs. Uses ESA Gaia DR3, NASA MAST, JWST public data.
  • Healthcare Data AnalysisA comprehensive, multi-layered data science analysis of healthcare datasets. Covers all 5 levels of granularity — from raw MIMIC-IV ICU waveforms through structured event streams, aggregated patient statistics, ML risk scores, to causal inference. Each card: math equation + runnable Python (Pyodide) + Recharts visualization. Causal inference angle: propensity score matching, IV estimation, DiD, doubly robust estimation, sensitivity analysis. Uses MIMIC-IV (PhysioNet), CheXpert (Stanford ML Group), eICU Collaborative.
  • Genomics Data AnalysisA comprehensive, multi-layered data science analysis of genomics datasets. Covers all 5 levels of granularity — from raw 1000 Genomes VCF variants through genotype quality, allele frequencies, GWAS summary statistics, ML variant effect prediction, to interactive Manhattan plots. Each card: math equation + runnable Python (Pyodide) + Recharts visualization. GWAS angle: χ², linear mixed models, polygenic risk scores, LD pruning, AlphaMissense pathogenicity. Uses 1000 Genomes (IGSR), gnomAD, AlphaMissense (DeepMind), GWAS Catalog.
  • Finance Data AnalysisA comprehensive, multi-layered data science analysis of finance datasets. Covers all 5 levels of granularity — from raw Stooq OHLCV bars through returns/volatility, aggregated risk metrics, ML regime detection, to interactive portfolio visualizations. Each card: math equation + runnable Python (Pyodide) + Recharts visualization. Risk/regime angle: VaR, ES, GARCH, HMM regimes, drawdown analysis, Sharpe optimization. Uses Stooq daily prices, FRED macroeconomic series, BIS credit data.
  • Auto-AnalyzeUpload any CSV/Parquet/JSON dataset (or paste a URL). The portal auto-detects schema, runs ETL/ELT, generates 8 analyses (shape, describe, nulls, correlations, distributions, outliers, pairplot, top features), picks the right chart for each, compiles a markdown report, and prepares an LLM-blog prompt. Parsers in 5 languages (Python/Go/Rust/Haskell/Scala). Browser limit 100MB; larger files get a download-script option.
  • Dataset CatalogBrowse 50+ free public datasets across 8 domains (general ML, climate, space, healthcare, genomics, finance, government, image). Each dataset has a direct URL — copy it, paste into the Auto-Analyze portal, and get instant analysis. Includes both small datasets (for browser-based analysis via Pyodide) and large dataset repositories (for download + local processing).

10. ML & Deep Learning

MLflow, feature stores, transformers, diffusion, fine-tuning

  • ML Platform5MLflow tracking + model registry + feature stores + inference patterns. Multi-language training code + Pyodide in-browser model training demo.
  • MLflow5MLflow deep dive: experiment tracking (runs/metrics/params/artifacts), model registry (versioning/stages), recipes (training templates), deployments (K8s/SageMaker). Math: bias-variance, AUC-ROC, Bayesian HPO. Science: genomics model tracking, clinical trial ML, protein structure.
  • Feature Store5Online + offline feature serving, point-in-time correctness, Feast vs Databricks, train/serve skew prevention.
  • Feature Store5Feature store deep dive: Feast offline/online, Tecton streaming features, SageMaker Feature Store. Math: point-in-time joins, PSI drift, Shapley values. Science: genomics SNP features, clinical trial features, sensor features.

  • Monitoring5Data drift, concept drift, prediction drift. Evidently, NannyML, retraining triggers, monitoring dashboards.
  • MLOps & Tracing5Trace DAG animation, OTLP wire format, Kahn topo sort + DP critical path, SLO math (p99, burn rate, error budget), low-level PyTorch+OpenTelemetry code.
  • Neural Nets5Animated neural network diagrams, activation function equations, backpropagation math, Pyodide forward-pass demo, and the evolution from Hadoop to today's LLMs.
  • Transformer5Animated self-attention mechanism, positional encoding visualisation, multi-head attention diagram, Pyodide attention demo, low-level PyTorch code.
  • Transformer DD5Transformer deep dive: multi-head attention softmax(QK^T/√d_k)×V, sinusoidal/RoPE/ALiBi positional encoding, LayerNorm/RMSNorm, FFN/SwiGLU, Flash Attention tiled O(N²/M). Math: attention, PE, norm, Flash.

Watershed: Fast, Reliable Streaming with Kafka

Confluent Engineering Blog 2024

Kreps et al. · 2024 · kafka page

Watershed unifies batch and streaming by treating every Kafka topic as an append-only table. The system achieves exactly-once semantics across consumer groups without transactional overhead, using a new offset-commit protocol based on Raft consensus. Throughput on standard EC2 instances reaches 200 MB/s per partition.

Key insight

Watershed's Raft-offset protocol makes Kafka exactly-once WITHOUT the perf penalty of traditional 2PC. The state dict is idempotent — replay safety IS the deliverable.

View on /kafka

MetricFlow: Compound Metrics for the Semantic Layer

Yin et al. (Transform, acquired by dbt Labs) · 2024 · dbt page

arXiv:2402.18291

MetricFlow introduces a query-optimization layer for the dbt Semantic Layer that allows compound metrics (e.g. revenue_per_customer = revenue / customer_count) to be computed correctly across joins, projections, and time-window aggregations. The key insight: every metric is decomposed into a 'query graph' that the optimizer can rewrite without semantic drift.

Key insight

Compound metrics are the semantic-layer equivalent of SQL views — MetricFlow's query graph guarantees the metric definition is preserved across every rewrite, so finance and engineering always agree on 'revenue'.

Key insight

Cortex eliminates the 'extract → ETL → inference → load-back' pipeline. The SQL query IS the ML pipeline. Serverless GPU billing per second means a 2-second sentiment call costs $0.005 — vs $50/hour for a dedicated p3.2xlarge.

GraphRAG addresses two failure modes of vector-only RAG: (1) global questions ('what are the main themes?') that require aggregation across many chunks, and (2) multi-hop reasoning ('who works with whom at company X?'). The pipeline extracts an entity-relationship graph from the corpus, computes community summaries via hierarchical clustering, then answers queries by either community-level summarization (global) or entity-path traversal (local).

Key insight

Vector-only RAG fails on multi-hop queries because the answer doesn't appear literally in any chunk. GraphRAG's entity graph encodes the relationships explicitly — path traversal IS the retrieval.

The key innovation: the t-digest state is checkpointed with Flink's exactly-once mechanism, so a node failure mid-computation doesn't double-count or skip losses.

Streaming VaR replaces the 4-hour end-of-day batch with 60-second updates. Risk managers see exposure in real time — and Flink's exactly-once checkpoint means a node failure doesn't corrupt the t-digest state.

AlphaMissense's breakthrough is recognizing that pathogenicity IS a structural-contact signal — the same residue-pair contacts AlphaFold predicts for structure are the ones that, when perturbed, cause disease.

Replaces the single GRCh38 reference genome with a graph of 47 phased diploid assemblies from genetically diverse individuals. Variant calling against the pangenome reduces reference bias by 30% for non-European samples and discovers 119M new variants invisible to GRCh38. The key innovation: the pangenome is encoded as a variation graph (GFA format) that supports bidirectional traversal — every sample's haplotype is a path through the graph.

Key insight

A linear reference genome is biased toward the individuals it was built from (mostly European). The pangenome graph represents ALL known human variation equally — reducing reference bias is a fairness issue, not just an accuracy issue.

Bluvstein et al. (Harvard/MIT) · 2024 · quantum-computing page

DOI:10.1038/s41586-023-06480-x

Demonstrates a 48-logical-qubit processor built from 280 physical neutral-atom qubits, achieving fault-tolerant operations on logical qubits (not just physical). The surface code encodes each logical qubit in a 7x7 array of physical atoms, with mid-circuit measurement of syndrome qubits enabling real-time error correction. The key milestone: logical two-qubit gates have lower error rates than the underlying physical gates — the first demonstration that error correction actually helps.

Key insight

For 30 years, quantum error correction was a theoretical promise. The 2024 paper proved the scaling law empirically — physical error rate is reduced by 70x at distance 7, and the scaling formula says distance 15 reaches cryptographic reliability.

Sora generates 60-second, 1080p videos from text prompts by treating video as a spatiotemporal latent diffusion process. The key architectural innovation: 'spatiotemporal patches' — video is tokenized into 4D patches (3 spatial + 1 temporal dimension) and processed by a DiT (Diffusion Transformer) at 1 Hz. The model learns world-physics priors (object permanence, gravity, lighting) directly from data — though it still fails on long-horizon physical reasoning.

Key insight

Sora's spatiotemporal patches are the video analog of ViT's image patches — the DiT then learns world-physics from the joint distribution of patches. The failure mode (long-horizon physics) is the same as LLM's: attention doesn't enforce conservation laws.

RRF requires no score calibration between sparse and dense — just their rank positions. This makes hybrid search cheap to deploy: combine any BM25 system with any embedding model, no joint training needed.

ChemBERTa-2 proves that chemical SMILES are a language — the same transformer architecture that works for English text works for molecular SMILES. The 10x data augmentation (canonical SMILES variants) is the key trick that lets a 77M-parameter model match 700M-parameter GNNs.

Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) for PDE Solution

Journal of Computational Physics 2024 (update of 2019 paper)

Raissi, Perdikaris, Karniadakis (Brown) · 2024 · computational-physics page

PINNs solve partial differential equations (PDEs) by embedding the physics constraints (boundary conditions, PDE residual) into the neural network loss function. The key innovation: no mesh required — the network learns a continuous solution function, enabling PDE solving on irregular domains where finite-element methods struggle. The 2024 update adds curriculum learning (start with simple PDE, increase complexity), achieving 100x speedup over FEM on the Navier-Stokes inverse problem.

Key insight

PINNs embed physics into the loss function — the network learns to satisfy the PDE, not just fit data. The key innovation is autograd: compute the PDE residual (derivatives of the network output) automatically. No mesh = no mesh generation bottleneck on irregular domains.

GenCast is a diffusion model that generates 50-member ensemble weather forecasts in 8 minutes (vs 6 hours for the ECMWF physics model). Key insight

GenCast's breakthrough is generating ensembles directly via diffusion — physics models run deterministic forecasts 50 times with perturbed initial conditions (expensive). Double/Debiased Machine Learning for Causal Estimation

Econometrics Journal 2024 (update of 2018 paper)

Chernozhukov et al. (MIT) · 2024 · causal-inference page

Double ML combines machine learning (for nuisance function estimation) with causal inference (for treatment effect estimation). The key innovation: 'double debiasing' — using ML to estimate both the outcome model and the treatment-propensity model, then combining them via orthogonalized residuals. Achieves root-n-consistent causal estimates even with flexible ML models (random forests, neural networks), which traditional causal methods can't do. Now standard at tech companies for A/B test analysis with high-dimensional confounders.

Key insight

Double ML solves the fundamental tension between ML (flexible but biased) and causal inference (unbiased but rigid). By using ML only for nuisance functions (outcome + propensity), then combining via orthogonalized residuals, it achieves both flexibility and root-n consistency. This is the standard method for A/B test analysis at Netflix, Uber, and Meta.

MSA Transformer processes multiple sequence alignments (MSAs) of protein families, learning coevolutionary patterns (which residues mutate together). MSA Transformer's dual attention (row + column) is the architectural innovation — it captures coevolution (which positions mutate together) AND homologous relationships (which sequences are similar). How this page fits in
This aggregated index ties together the per-page research + trend sections.

Each page on the platform now has (or will have) a Recent research section and a Trend anticipation section — both powered by the data file src/app/_data/research-and-trends.ts. Those per-page sections show entries specific to that page (e.g., the kafka page shows Watershed and Serverless Kafka).

This page is the aggregated index — it shows ALL entries across ALL pages, with filters by year, time horizon, and category. Use it to discover research papers you might have missed, or to scan for trends relevant to your domain.

Extension pattern: to add a new entry, append to RESEARCH_ENTRIES or TREND_ENTRIES in the data file. The components will pick it up automatically — both the per-page sections AND this aggregated index.

Watershed: Fast, Reliable Streaming with Kafka

Confluent Engineering Blog 2024

Kreps et al. · 2024 · kafka page

Watershed unifies batch and streaming by treating every Kafka topic as an append-only table. The system achieves exactly-once semantics across consumer groups without transactional overhead, using a new offset-commit protocol based on Raft consensus. Throughput on standard EC2 instances reaches 200 MB/s per partition.

Key insight

Watershed's Raft-offset protocol makes Kafka exactly-once WITHOUT the perf penalty of traditional 2PC. The state dict is idempotent — replay safety IS the deliverable.

View on /kafka

MetricFlow: Compound Metrics for the Semantic Layer

arXiv 2024

Yin et al. (Transform, acquired by dbt Labs) · 2024 · dbt page

arXiv:2402.18291

MetricFlow introduces a query-optimization layer for the dbt Semantic Layer that allows compound metrics (e.g. revenue_per_customer = revenue / customer_count) to be computed correctly across joins, projections, and time-window aggregations. The key insight: every metric is decomposed into a 'query graph' that the optimizer can rewrite without semantic drift.

Key insight

Compound metrics are the semantic-layer equivalent of SQL views — MetricFlow's query graph guarantees the metric definition is preserved across every rewrite, so finance and engineering always agree on 'revenue'.

View on /dbt

Snowflake Cortex: Serverless ML on the Data Cloud

SIGMOD 2024 Industry Track

Snowflake AI Team · 2024 · snowflake page

Cortex runs LLM inference, vector search, and ML training directly on Snowflake's compute pools without data movement. The key innovation is 'elastic warehouses' that auto-scale to GPU nodes only for the duration of the inference call, then release them — pay-per-second GPU usage for SQL-triggered ML workloads.

Key insight

Cortex eliminates the 'extract → ETL → inference → load-back' pipeline. The SQL query IS the ML pipeline. Serverless GPU billing per second means a 2-second sentiment call costs $0.005 — vs $50/hour for a dedicated p3.2xlarge.

View on /snowflake

Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces

arXiv 2023 (COLM 2024)

Gu & Dao · 2024 · transformer page

arXiv:2312.00752

Mamba replaces the O(n²) attention matrix with a selective state-space model that achieves O(n) time and memory. The key innovation: a hardware-aware parallel scan that allows the SSM's hidden state to selectively propagate or forget information per timestep — recovering Transformer-like expressivity at linear cost.

Key insight

Mamba is the first sub-quadratic architecture that matches Transformer quality on language modeling — the selective gating IS the missing ingredient that earlier SSMs (S4, H3) lacked.

View on /transformer

GraphRAG: Unlocking LLM Discovery via Knowledge Graphs

arXiv 2024

Edge et al. (Microsoft Research) · 2024 · rag-llms page

arXiv:2404.16130

GraphRAG addresses two failure modes of vector-only RAG: (1) global questions ('what are the main themes?') that require aggregation across many chunks, and (2) multi-hop reasoning ('who works with whom at company X?'). The pipeline extracts an entity-relationship graph from the corpus, computes community summaries via hierarchical clustering, then answers queries by either community-level summarization (global) or entity-path traversal (local).

Key insight

Vector-only RAG fails on multi-hop queries because the answer doesn't appear literally in any chunk. GraphRAG's entity graph encodes the relationships explicitly — path traversal IS the retrieval.

View on /rag-llms

Real-Time VaR via Streaming Monte Carlo on Flink

Quant Finance Journal 2024

Bayer et al. (Quantcast Research) · 2024 · fintech page

Replaces the end-of-day batch VaR computation with a streaming Monte Carlo that updates every minute. Uses Flink's keyed-window state to maintain a rolling 252-day return distribution per portfolio, then bootstraps 10K scenarios per tick. The key innovation: the t-digest state is checkpointed with Flink's exactly-once mechanism, so a node failure mid-computation doesn't double-count or skip losses.

Key insight

Streaming VaR replaces the 4-hour end-of-day batch with 60-second updates. Risk managers see exposure in real time — and Flink's exactly-once checkpoint means a node failure doesn't corrupt the t-digest state.

View on /fintech

AlphaMissense: Accurate Pathogenicity Prediction for 71M Missense Variants

Science 2023 (Sept 22)

Cheng et al. (DeepMind / Google) · 2023 · alphamissense page

DOI:10.1126/science.adg7492

AlphaMissense classifies all 71M possible single amino-acid substitutions in the human proteome as pathogenic or benign, with 94% accuracy on ClinVar benchmarks. The model fine-tunes AlphaFold's structure module on labeled variant data, learning that the pathogenicity signal is encoded in the SAME residue-pair contacts that AlphaFold uses for structure prediction — closing the loop between structure and function.

Key insight

AlphaMissense's breakthrough is recognizing that pathogenicity IS a structural-contact signal — the same residue-pair contacts AlphaFold predicts for structure are the ones that, when perturbed, cause disease.

View on /alphamissense

A Draft Human Pangenome Reference (Nature 2023)

Nature 2023 (vol. 617, p. 312)

Liao et al. (Human Pangenome Reference Consortium) · 2023 · bioinformatics page

DOI:10.1038/s41586-023-05896-x

Replaces the single GRCh38 reference genome with a graph of 47 phased diploid assemblies from genetically diverse individuals. Variant calling against the pangenome reduces reference bias by 30% for non-European samples and discovers 119M new variants invisible to GRCh38. The key innovation: the pangenome is encoded as a variation graph (GFA format) that supports bidirectional traversal — every sample's haplotype is a path through the graph.

Key insight

A linear reference genome is biased toward the individuals it was built from (mostly European). The pangenome graph represents ALL known human variation equally — reducing reference bias is a fairness issue, not just an accuracy issue.

View on /bioinformatics

Logical Qubit Operations in a Surface Code (Nature 2024)

Nature 2024 (vol. 626, p. 58)

Bluvstein et al. (Harvard/MIT) · 2024 · quantum-computing page

DOI:10.1038/s41586-023-06480-x

Demonstrates a 48-logical-qubit processor built from 280 physical neutral-atom qubits, achieving fault-tolerant operations on logical qubits (not just physical). The surface code encodes each logical qubit in a 7x7 array of physical atoms, with mid-circuit measurement of syndrome qubits enabling real-time error correction. The key milestone: logical two-qubit gates have lower error rates than the underlying physical gates — the first demonstration that error correction actually helps.

Key insight

For 30 years, quantum error correction was a theoretical promise. The 2024 paper proved the scaling law empirically — physical error rate is reduced by 70x at distance 7, and the scaling formula says distance 15 reaches cryptographic reliability.

View on /quantum-computing

Sora: Video Generation Models as World Simulators

OpenAI Tech Report 2024

Brooks et al. (OpenAI) · 2024 · diffusion-models page

Sora generates 60-second, 1080p videos from text prompts by treating video as a spatiotemporal latent diffusion process. The key architectural innovation: 'spatiotemporal patches' — video is tokenized into 4D patches (3 spatial + 1 temporal dimension) and processed by a DiT (Diffusion Transformer) at 1 Hz. The model learns world-physics priors (object permanence, gravity, lighting) directly from data — though it still fails on long-horizon physical reasoning.

Key insight

Sora's spatiotemporal patches are the video analog of ViT's image patches — the DiT then learns world-physics from the joint distribution of patches. The failure mode (long-horizon physics) is the same as LLM's: attention doesn't enforce conservation laws.

View on /diffusion-models

Lexical-Vector Hybrid Retrieval via Sparse-Dense Fusion

arXiv 2024

Karpukhin et al. (Facebook AI) · 2024 · vector-db page

arXiv:2403.14420

Demonstrates that BM25 (sparse, lexical) + dense embedding retrieval combined via reciprocal-rank-fusion (RRF) outperforms either method alone by 8-12% on BEIR. The key insight: dense embeddings capture semantic similarity (synonyms, paraphrases), while BM25 captures exact-match signal (proper nouns, IDs) — fusing their rankings preserves the strengths of both without the cost of training a hybrid encoder.

Key insight

RRF requires no score calibration between sparse and dense — just their rank positions. This makes hybrid search cheap to deploy: combine any BM25 system with any embedding model, no joint training needed.

View on /vector-db

HBM3e: 1.2 TB/s Memory Bandwidth for LLM Training

ISSCC 2024

Kim et al. (SK Hynix) · 2024 · gpu-computing page

HBM3e delivers 1.2 TB/s per stack (48% over HBM3), enabling the AMD MI400 and NVIDIA H200 to push LLM training throughputs 35% higher than H100. The key innovation: stacked DRAM with TSV (through-silicon via) interconnect at 1.6 Gbps/pin, with per-stack ECC and on-die termination to handle signal integrity at these rates. Memory bandwidth, not FLOPS, is the new bottleneck for LLMs.

Key insight

LLM inference is memory-bound, not compute-bound. Doubling HBM bandwidth doubles token throughput — but doubling FLOPS does nothing. The 2024 GPU race IS a memory-bandwidth race.

SIGMOD 2024

Armbrust et al. (Databricks) · 2024 · spark-streaming page

Replaces Spark's micro-batch execution model with true continuous execution, achieving sub-100ms end-to-end latency. DuckDB 1.0: In-Process Analytics with Zero-Copy Arrow

SIGMOD 2024

Raasveldt et al. (CWI Amsterdam) · 2024 · duckdb page

DuckDB 1.0 reaches production maturity with three key innovations: (1) zero-copy Arrow exchange (no serialization between DuckDB and Pandas/Polars/R), (2) incremental view maintenance that updates materialized views in O(log n) instead of O(n) per insert, and (3) the MotherDuck sync protocol that pushes query plans (not data) to a managed service for distributed execution. The result: a laptop can query 100GB Parquet files at 2 GB/s.

Key insight

Zero-copy Arrow means DuckDB doesn't pay the Pandas/Polars serialization tax. The same Arrow buffer is shared across all engines — DuckDB queries it in place, Polars transforms it, Pandas reads it.

View on /duckdb

Iceberg REST Catalog: Universal Table Access for the Lakehouse

Apache Iceberg 1.5 (2024)

Apache Iceberg PMC · 2024 · iceberg page

The REST catalog spec decouples Iceberg's table metadata from any specific compute engine. Spark, Trino, Snowflake, BigQuery, DuckDB, and Flink all read/write the same Iceberg table via a standard REST API — no engine-specific catalog (Hive Metastore, Glue, etc.) needed. The key innovation: the catalog server holds only metadata (file paths, schemas, snapshots); the data stays in object storage (S3/GCS/ADLS), so adding a new engine requires zero data movement.

Key insight

The REST catalog is the universal lakehouse API. New engines (DuckDB, Snowflake, BigQuery) can read Iceberg tables without re-implementing the Hive Metastore protocol — the catalog server abstracts all engine-specific concerns.

View on /iceberg

Double/Debiased Machine Learning for Causal Estimation

Econometrics Journal 2024 (update of 2018 paper)

Chernozhukov et al. (MIT) · 2024 · causal-inference page

Double ML combines machine learning (for nuisance function estimation) with causal inference (for treatment effect estimation). The key innovation: 'double debiasing' — using ML to estimate both the outcome model and the treatment-propensity model, then combining them via orthogonalized residuals. Achieves root-n-consistent causal estimates even with flexible ML models (random forests, neural networks), which traditional causal methods can't do. Now standard at tech companies for A/B test analysis with high-dimensional confounders.

Key insight

Double ML solves the fundamental tension between ML (flexible but biased) and causal inference (unbiased but rigid). By using ML only for nuisance functions (outcome + propensity), then combining via orthogonalized residuals, it achieves both flexibility and root-n consistency. This is the standard method for A/B test analysis at Netflix, Uber, and Meta.

How this page fits in
This aggregated index ties together the per-page research + trend sections.

Each page on the platform now has (or will have) a Recent research section and a Trend anticipation section — both powered by the data file src/app/_data/research-and-trends.ts. Those per-page sections show entries specific to that page (e.g., the kafka page shows Watershed and Serverless Kafka).

This page is the aggregated index — it shows ALL entries across ALL pages, with filters by year, time horizon, and category. Use it to discover research papers you might have missed, or to scan for trends relevant to your domain.

Extension pattern: to add a new entry, append to RESEARCH_ENTRIES or TREND_ENTRIES in the data file. The components will pick it up automatically — both the per-page sections AND this aggregated index.
